title: Write a HorizontalPodAutoscaler
intro: 'kubectl autoscale' (tutorial-013) only covers the simple case. The YAML form is what you commit to git and extend with scaling behavior.

steps.prompt: Write an autoscaling/v2 HorizontalPodAutoscaler named 'web' that targets the Deployment 'web' (apiVersion apps/v1), scales between 2 and 10 replicas, and targets 70% average CPU utilization (a Resource metric).
steps.hint: spec.scaleTargetRef identifies what to scale (apiVersion, kind, name). spec.metrics is a list; a CPU metric is: type: Resource, resource: {name: cpu, target: {type: Utilization, averageUtilization: 70}}.
steps.solution:
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: web
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: web
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 10
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 70
steps.explanation: The HPA adds or removes web replicas to keep average CPU near 70% of each pod's CPU REQUEST.
steps.why: Utilization is measured against resources.requests, so this HPA does nothing useful if the Deployment has no CPU request — and it needs metrics-server running at all (see incident-009, where a missing metrics-server left an HPA silently stuck). minReplicas: 2 keeps a spare pod for availability even at zero traffic.
